slides.title: The big idea
slides.html:
Triangle Angle Bisector Theorem: the bisector of an angle of a triangle divides the opposite side into segments proportional to the other two sides.

In triangle ABC, if AD bisects angle A with D on BC, then BD/DC = AB/AC.

Proof: draw the line through C parallel to AD, meeting line AB at E. Then angle ACE = angle CAD and angle AEC = angle BAD, which are equal, so triangle ACE is isosceles with AE = AC. By the Side-Splitter Theorem in triangle BCE, BD/DC = BA/AE = AB/AC.
